hyps.why: Increasing an already large learning rate pushes Adam training into instability, so the gain turns into a loss.
At very small learning rates the network is undertrained in 243 epochs, so increasing the rate helps most there.
Large batches mean fewer updates, so a larger step size compensates more.
Reducing a divergent learning rate recovers accuracy.
Lowering an already tiny learning rate deepens undertraining.
With a low learning rate, fewer updates per epoch make undertraining worse.
Larger batches reduce gradient noise and stabilize training at high learning rates.
Raising an already strong L2 penalty causes severe underfitting, whereas at small alpha it is negligible.
Deeper ReLU networks are more prone to divergence and dead units under large learning rates.
Wider layers amplify effective update size, so widening hurts or helps less when the learning rate is already high.
